content.title: About
content.content: Horseradish is the root of the plant Armoracia rusticana, native to Eastern Europe and Western Asia. It has a sharp, pungent flavor and is used as a condiment, in pickles, and as an ingredient in sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Horseradish belongs to the Brassicaceae family and is related to cabbage, radish, and mustard.
Traditionally it has been used in folk medicine to stimulate digestion and as a remedy for colds.
High glucosinolate content gives horseradish natural antiseptic properties.
In many countries it is served with meat dishes, especially beef and pork, and with sauerkraut.
Freshly grated horseradish can retain its heat for 2–3 weeks when stored properly.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Glucosinolates and vitamin C in horseradish help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The sharp taste stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory effects
items.content: Extracts of horseradish have been shown to reduce inflammatory markers.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and phytochemicals strengthen the body's defense mechanisms.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: The intense heat can cause discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to Brassicaceae plants.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Large amounts may enhance the effect of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Excessive consumption of very spicy horseradish in the first trimester is not recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Horseradish is typically grated and added to sauces, marinades, sauerkraut, or used as a condiment for meat dishes. It can also be pickled in vinegar or preserved in a sweet syrup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the root in the refrigerator wrapped in a paper towel inside an airtight container – up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze grated horseradish in small portions.
